correctness.rationale: For 1<p<infinity, the sharp coefficient functional is integration of the boundary trace against a two-frequency kernel. Because the sharp constant exceeds one, neither target coefficient can vanish at equality, and strict complex Holder equality forces the boundary trace to be a phase-scaled sign(cos)|cos|^{1/(p-1)} profile; direct integration proves the converse. The Fourier spectrum follows from the exact recurrence (m+r+1)c_{m+1}=(r+1-m)c_{m-1}; iteration yields the Gamma formula and shows termination exactly when r is a positive odd integer. If r is not such an integer every positive odd mode is nonzero. The classified continuous trace at index n has exactly 2n zeros, so the same nonzero function cannot extremize a different index. Fresh numerical integration for several noninteger and odd-integer r values independently matched the Gamma coefficients and pole-induced truncation.

originality.rationale: The complete Chen--Huang--Jin--Li paper was read. Its Theorem 1.3 proves the sharp constant and its proof constructs exactly one cosine-power Poisson witness, but it does not state the converse equality classification, the full Fourier spectrum of every extremizer, the finite-spectrum phase, or rigidity across coefficient indices. Pages 13--15 complete the witness calculation and references without adding such a classification. Earlier p=infinity extremal classifications concern a different endpoint inequality. Resultary searches found the assigned result but no prior theorem with the same all-extremizer consequences.

value.rationale: Classifying equality cases is the natural structural question immediately after a sharp constant is established. Here the classification yields nontrivial extra information: the complete analytic/coanalytic spectrum, a discrete finite-spectrum phase in p, and impossibility of simultaneous extremality at two coefficient indices. These are exact structural consequences not visible from merely exhibiting one sharpness witness.

limitations: Restricted to 1<p<infinity; the p=1 endpoint is not classified.
The result does not improve the sharp constant and gives no quantitative stability theorem for near-extremizers.
